title: Order No. T-37789 — Transportation Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission vs. Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace's Towing & Transport.
text:
Order No. T-37789 
Page 1 of 11 
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 

ORDER NUMBER T-37789 

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
VERSUS 
RODNEY DUPRE, JR. DBA JACE’S TOWING & TRANSPORT 

Docket No. T-37789, In re: Alleged violation of (1) 45:161 through 180.1 and General Order 
dated November 8, 1999, by operating Intrastate without LPSC authority and (2) General Order 
dated December 20, 2024 for exceeding state prescribed rates, allegedly having occurred on or 
about October 04, 2025. 

(Decided at the June 17, 2026 Business and Executive Session.) 

ORDER 

Overview 
The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) issued a citation 
dated November 25, 2025, to Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s Towing & Transport (“Jace’s Towing” 
or the “Carrier”). The citation directs the Carrier to appear at a hearing on February 3, 2026, to 
show cause why it should not be found guilty as alleged in the In re. The citation was docketed as 
the instant proceeding and notice of this proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official 
Bulletin dated December 5, 2025. When the hearing was convened on February 3, 2026, 
Commission Staff appeared through counsel and presented testimonial and documentary evidence 
in support of its allegations. The Carrier did not appear at the hearing. For the reasons stated herein, 
we find Jace’s Towing guilty as alleged. 

The Recommendation of the Administrative Law Judge (Corrected) (“Recommendation”) 
was issued in the form of a Draft Order on June 5, 2026. The Recommendation was considered at 
the Commission’s Business and Executive Session held on June 17, 2026. On motion of 
Commissioner Lewis, seconded by Vice Chairman Coussan, with Chairman Skrmetta concurring 
and Commissioner Campbell absent, the Commission accepted the Recommendation. 
Applicable Law 

The Commission exercises jurisdiction in this proceeding pursuant to Article IV, Section 
21 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, which provides in pertinent part: 
The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public 
utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. 
It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and 
procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and perform 
other duties as provided by law. 

In addition, the Louisiana Legislature, in La. R.S. 45:163, delegates certain authority to the 
Commission over motor carriers operating intrastate in Louisiana. La. R.S. 45:162(12) includes 
tow trucks in the definition of “motor carriers” subject to the Commission’s regulation. More 
specifically, the Louisiana Legislature has declared, in La. R.S. 45:180.1, that the “use and 
operation of wreckers and towing services should be the subject of regulation by the Louisiana 
Public Service Commission,”1 and that the Commission has “the power and authority necessary to 
supervise, govern, regulate, and control the business of the operation and use of wreckers and 
towing services . . . [and] to fix reasonable and just rates, fares, tolls, charges for storage services 

1 La. R.S. 45:180.1(B). 
Order No. T-37789 
Page 2 of 11 
. . . .”2 In accordance with La. R.S. 45:171(A), no carrier shall violate the provisions of Title 45, 
Chapter 4 (which includes La. R.S. 45: 180.1) or any Commission order. La. R.S. 45:180.1 states 
that in addition to any other penalties imposed by Chapter 4, no person shall violate Section 180.1 
or engage in the operation and use of wreckers and towing services without first having obtained 
authority from the Commission. La. R.S. 45:171(C) and La. R.S. 45:180.1(E) state that violators 
shall be fined by the Commission at open hearing not less than $100 and not more than $10,000. 

Pursuant to these delegations of authority, the Commission adopted rules applicable to 
wrecker and towing services providing nonconsensual towing and recovery services. The 
Commission’s General Order dated November 8, 1999 (“1999 General Order”),3 adopted 
guidelines for nonconsensual wrecker and towing services, including an application process. 
Section II, General Requirements for Wrecker and Towing Services within the State of Louisiana, 
states that an application will be submitted, and upon Staff approval applicants must comply with 
the requirements of R.S. 45:161 through 172 before a certificate or permit will be issued. Section 
II also specifies the insurance requirements. While Section II of the 1999 General Order remains 
intact, the rates and terms applicable to nonconsensual towing and recovery services have been 
amended many times since the issuance of the 1999 General Order. 

The most recent General Order addressing nonconsensual towing and recovery service 
rates is the Commission’s General Order dated December 20, 2024 (“Towing Order”).4 Amended 
Attachment A to the Towing Order includes the schedule of the rates and terms for nonconsensual 
towing and recovery services applicable to Commission-jurisdictional carriers. Included therein at 
Section VII, Annual Producer Price Index Adjustment, it states that the LPSC’s rates will be 
increased or decreased annually based on the Producer Price Index (“PPI”), that the rate change 
will be posted on the Commission’s website each April 1, and that the rates will become effective 
upon posting. Pursuant to the Towing Order, the rates and terms that apply to the tow at issue in 
this proceeding are found in Amended Attachment A for 2024 PPI to the General Order updated 
on April 1, 2025 (“2025 Towing Order Rates”).5 The most pertinent terms and rates to the issues 
of the case are as follows: 
Amended Attachment A for 2024 PPI to the General Order 

SCHEDULE OF PRESCRIBED RATES AND REQUIREMENTS FOR 
NON-CONSENSUAL TOWING, RECOVERY AND RELATED SERVICES 

I. 
DEFINITIONS 
. . . 
Q. Tow - a standard tow that does not require special techniques or special equipment as 
defined in Recovery but does require normal use of tow sling, wheel lift, or winch cable to 
winch a vehicle onto a tilt bed tow truck. Tow rates shall apply whether the vehicle is either 
mobile or immobile and is in contact of the roadway surface. 

1. Non-consensual towing - the movement or transportation of a vehicle by a tow truck 
without the prior consent or authorization of the owner or operator of the vehicle. 
This includes private property tows conducted in accordance with the provisions of 
R.S. 32:1736 and tows by law enforcement or other public agencies. Whenever an 
owner or operator of a vehicle requests a law enforcement officer or other public 
agency to initiate a tow, such tow shall be considered non-consensual and subject 
to Louisiana Public Service Commission tow rates.

legislation applicable to the LPSC’s jurisdiction over towing and wrecker services. 
4 General Order 12-20-2024 (R-35595) - Corrected, dated December 20, 2024, Louisiana Public Service Commission,

1. Light Duty - the towing, transport, and recovery of a vehicle with a gross vehicle 
weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less.

II. 
RATES 

A. TOWING, RECOVERY, TRANSIT TIME 

Towing rates start at time of dispatch, and end when the vehicle reaches the tow companies 
[sic] storage facility or is released to the vehicle owner without being stored. 
. . . 

Private Property Tow 
Light Duty - $146.50 flat rate; or $179.00 flat rate when repositioning equipment, a 
fold down light bar, or an additional operator is required. The Tow Company must 
document why repositioning equipment, a fold down light bar or additional operator is 
required. 
. . . 
. . . 

D. FUEL SURCHARGE 

A Tow Company shall apply the fuel surcharge on the sum of the towing, recovery, 
transit time, and extra truck and trailer charges only. 
Fuel Price (per gallon) 
Fuel Surcharge 
$0.00 to $1.24 No surcharge 
$1.25 to $1.99 3% surcharge 
$2.00 to $2.99 9% surcharge 
$3.00 to $3.99 12% surcharge 
$4.00 to $4.99 14% surcharge 
$5.00 and greater 
16% surcharge 
There shall be no change in the top portion of the brackets. If fuel ever returns to the 
$1.24 level and below, a surcharge shall not be charged. The surcharge will be based 
on the average price of U.S. On-Highway Diesel Fuel as determined based upon the 
price reported by the Energy Information Administration (“eia”) for the Petroleum 
Administration for Gulf Coast (PADD3). 

E. GENERAL PROVISIONS 

1. A Tow Company shall only charge the rates stated in this order and fees allowed by 
State Police in LAC Title 55. 

2. All rates for towing, recovery, and stand-by in Section II.A and B include the truck and 
driver. 

3. A Tow Company shall only charge for equipment and personnel that are present at the 
scene of the recovery or tow. 

4. The Commission’s jurisdiction is from the time that the towing or recovery unit is 
dispatched to provide the non-consensual tow service until the time the vehicle is 
released to the owner (or authorized representative) of the vehicle. The tow company 
shall not charge any rate other than those specified in this order , for removal of debris 
from the scene, for draining fluids (with the exception of draining damaged fuel tanks 
to prevent fuel from leaking during towing and billed pursuant to Section B. 
Specialized Labor, Equipment or Services), removing batteries, or other similar activity 
aimed at preventing the vehicle from leaking. 
Order No. T-37789 
Page 4 of 11 
. . . 
VI. 
COMPLAINTS AND FINES 
. . . 
B. In addition to any fines authorized by La. R.S. Title 45 or Commission Orders, the 
Commission may order a refund of up to 200% of any overcharges. 

VII. 
ANNUAL PRODUCER PRICE INDEX ADJUSTMENT 
Commission Staff will calculate the annual change in Producer Price Index (“PPI”), as 
determined by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, that will be allowed to be applied to the 
LPSC’s rates for nonconsensual towing services. The LPSC’s rates will be increased or 
decreased by an amount equal to the annual percentage rate change (rounded to the nearest 
$0.50). The rate change will be posted annually on the LPSC’s website on April 1st, or the 
next business day following. Any rate increase or decrease pursuant to this section shall be 
effective upon posting by the Commission Staff. 

******************** 
The Commission’s General Order dated June 7, 20066 (“2006 General Order”), authorizes 
the imposition of a $25 citation fee when a citation is issued to a Commission-jurisdictional motor 
carrier. 
The Commission Staff’s Case 

At the hearing and in LPSC Staff’s Post-Hearing Brief (“Post-Hearing Brief”), 
Commission Staff alleged that Jace’s Towing violated La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1 and the 1999 
General Order by operating intrastate without authority, and violated the Towing Order by 
exceeding state prescribed rates contained in the 2025 Towing Order Rates. Commission Staff 
seeks an order: 1) finding the Jace’s Towing guilty as alleged; 2) fining Jace’s Towing $1000 
pursuant to La. R.S. 45:171(C) and 180.1(E) for operating without authority;7 3) requiring Jace’s 
Towing to refund $171.84 to the complainant pursuant to the Towing Order/2025 Towing Order 
Rates;8 and, 4) requiring Jace’s Towing to pay a $25 citation fee per the 2006 General Order. In 
support of its allegations, the Commission Staff presented the testimony of Transportation 
Administrator Tammy Burl. 
Testimony of Tammy Burl 
Ms. Burl testified that as Transportation Administrator she supervises the day-to-day 
operations of the Commission’s Transportation Division, including complaints and investigations 
into carriers who may be operating without authority and exceeding state prescribed rates. Ms. 
Burl testified to her knowledge of applicable statutes and General Orders regarding nonconsensual 
towing. She stated that pursuant to the Towing Order, rates may be increased on April 1 each year 
and the revised rates are posted on the Commission’s website. She stated further that rates were 
increased on April 1, 2025. 

Ms. Burl testified that she was familiar with Jace’s Towing because it was previously 
registered with the Commission as a nonconsensual towing company, but was no longer registered. 
She identified a letter, dated September 27, 2023, to Jace’s Towing stating that it advised the 
Carrier that its LPSC account was closed effective September 25, 2023, and that it was no longer 
allowed to perform nonconsensual tows in Louisiana. Also, that if Jace’s Towing wanted to resume 
operations, the letter provided the steps necessary to reinstate its LPSC authority. Attached to the 
letter was a copy of Order No. T-36898 dated September 25, 2023, ordering the cancellation of 
Common Carrier Certificate No. 7922-A, previously issued to Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s

Towing & Transport.9 Per Ms. Burl, the letter, with Order No. T-36898 attached, was mailed and 
emailed to Jace’s Towing on September 27, 2023. 

According to Ms. Burl, on or about October 4, 2025, Maegan Cline submitted a complaint 
to the Transportation Division through the online complaint email system indicating that Jace’s 
Towing had towed her Hyundai Elantra on October 4, 2025 (“Complaint”). Ms. Burl identified the 
Complaint and read from Ms. Cline’s description of the events surrounding the tow contained in 
the Complaint. Notably, that Ms. Cline indicated in the Complaint that her teenage daughter was 
driving the Elantra and parked at an event in Opelousas. Upon leaving the event around 10:00 
P.M., Jace’s Towing was in the process of towing the Elantra. Ms. Cline spoke to the driver of the 
tow truck by telephone, paid the tow truck driver $250 through CashApp, and the tow truck driver 
unhooked the Elantra. After receiving the Complaint, Ms. Burl began investigating Jace’s Towing. 

Ms. Burl stated that subsequent to receiving the Complaint, she contacted Ms. Cline and 
discussed the Complaint with her. Ms. Burl testified that Ms. Cline told her that she had disputed 
the charge with CashApp, but the dispute was denied. Following this conversation, Ms. Cline 
submitted a series of documents to Ms. Burl through the online complaint email system. Ms. Burl 
identified a series of documents as the documents provided to her by Ms. Cline, describing them 
as: a photo of the tow invoice for the tow (Invoice #563); a screenshot of the CashApp payment 
made by Ms. Cline to Rodney Dupre, Jr. showing date/time as October 4 at 10:19 P.M (including 
a reference to the denied dispute with CashApp); a photo of the car that was towed; a screenshot 
of a map showing the location of where the car was parked at the time of the tow; and a picture 
taken at the scene of the tow.10 

Per Ms. Burl, she reviewed Commission records for Jace’s Towing, including Order No. 
T-36898 and the related correspondence to the Carrier. She then contacted Louisiana State Police 
(“LSP”) and spoke to Sergeant Luquette and Trooper Soileau of the LSP Towing and Recovery 
Division, who advised her that LSP had also received a complaint from Ms. Cline regarding the 
tow (“Complaint to LSP”), and that LSP’s investigation was ongoing. Ms. Burl identified a Facility 
Inspection Report dated November 4, 2025 (“LSP Report”), which she stated contained the results 
of the LSP’s investigation into the Complaint to LSP. Ms. Burl advised that the LSP Report was 
transmitted to her by Sergeant Luquette about a week after November 4, 2025, once it was 
uploaded into LSP’s main system. Ms. Burl then read from the LSP Report, stating that it indicated 
that LSP would be citing Jace’s Towing for violations related to the Complaint to LSP. Ms. Burl 
testified that the LSP was citing Jace’s Towing for certain violations and deferring other charges 
to the LPSC, based on LPSC jurisdiction.11 

Ms. Burl testified that, after receiving the LSP Report, she spoke to Sergeant Luquette and 
Trooper Soileau confirming the contents of the LSP Report. Ms. Burl advised Sergeant Luquette 
and Trooper Soileau that the LPSC would be issuing a citation to Jace’s Towing. Ms. Burl then 
identified the citation issued to Jace’s Towing, advising that it directed Jace’s Towing to appear at 
a hearing on February 3, 2026, and that attached to the citation were the Complaint and the LSP 
Report. She indicated that the citation was prepared for her signature by her staff under her 
direction. Per Ms. Burl, the citation was mailed to the Carrier via United States Postal Service 
(“USPS”) certified mail on November 25, 2025, at the address provided by Ms. Cline in the 
Complaint. Ms. Burl noted that address matched the address on file for the Carrier when it last

held LPSC authority and the address listed for the Carrier in the LSP Report. She confirmed that 
notice of the citation was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin dated December 5, 2025. 

Mr. Burl stated that the citation sent by certified mail was claimed, and identified a signed 
certified mail receipt with the last six digits 613985. She stated that those six digits matched the 
last six digits on the certified tracking number listed on the citation. Ms. Burl noted that the receipt 
did not have a date of delivery, but bore a stamp from the USPS in Opelousas dated January 20, 
2026. The receipt was stamped received by the Commission’s Transportation Division on January 
27, 2026. 

Ms. Burl testified that prior to the issuance of the citation, and to her recollection sometime 
between October 30 and November 3, [2025], Mr. Dupre reached out to her regarding the process 
for reinstating his authority. She stated that she forwarded him the email sent back on September 
27, 2023, after verbally confirming his email address, and offered to answer any questions he may 
have about the process. She did not hear from him after that phone conversation. 

Per Ms. Burl, the subject tow would be considered a light-duty, private property tow, and 
per the 2025 Towing Order Rates, the rate should have been a flat rate of $146.50, plus a 12% fuel 
surcharge and no additional charges.12 Ms. Burl stated that she reviewed the price of fuel for the 
week of the tow per the Gulf Coast PADD 3 region (as per the 2025 Towing Order Rates), and the 
applicable fuel charge would have been 12%.13 

Ms. Burl reiterated that the Commission Staff is seeking that Jace’s Towing be found guilty 
of violating La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1 and the 1999 General Order for operating intrastate 
without LPSC authority and violating the Towing Order for exceeding state prescribed rates as 
found in the 2025 Towing Order Rates. Ms. Burl stated that Commission Staff is seeking a guilty 
finding, and that Jace’s Towing be ordered to refund 200% of the overcharge to Ms. Cline as the 
Towing Order permits a refund of up to 200% of the overcharge, and that it was warranted based 
on the facts of this case.14 Additionally, Commission Staff requests that Jace’s Towing be fined 
$1000 and assessed the $25 citation fee pursuant to the 2006 General Order.

At the conclusion of the presentation of its evidence, Commission Staff reiterated its 
requested relief in this matter. The Tribunal requested that Commission Staff submit a post-hearing 
brief. Consistent with discussions at hearing, on February 25, 2026, the Tribunal issued a Notice 
of Transcript Availability and Notice of Post-Hearing Briefing Deadline setting the deadline for 
March 18, 2026. Commission Staff filed LPSC Staff’s Post-Hearing Brief on March 18, 2026, 
providing clarifying and additional legal support for its allegations and requested relief. 
Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law 
Having considered applicable law and the evidence presented in this case, the Commission 
makes the following findings of fact and conclusions of law: 
Findings of Fact 
1. Jace’s Towing previously held LPSC authority to perform nonconsensual tows through 
Common Carrier Certificate No. 7922-A. Jace’s Towing’s authority was canceled by Order 
No. T-36898 issued on September 25, 2023. 
2. On September 27, 2023, Ms. Burl mailed and emailed a letter to Jace’s Towing explaining 
that its authority had been canceled, it was no longer permitted to conduct nonconsensual 
tows in Louisiana, and the steps necessary to reinstate its authority if it wished to resume 
operations. Attached was a copy of Order No. T-36898 (Staff Exhibit 1, in globo). 
3. Jace’s Towing did not have LPSC authority to perform nonconsensual tows on October 4, 
2025, and as of the date of the hearing, had not obtained authority. 
Order No. T-37789 
Page 8 of 11 
4. On October 4, 2025, Maegan Cline’s daughter parked a Hyundai Elantra in Opelousas, 
Louisiana to attend an event. 
5. Around 10:19 P.M., upon Ms. Cline’s daughter’s return to the Elantra, Jace’s Towing had 
the Elantra hooked to a tow truck and was in the process of towing or preparing to tow the 
Elantra. 
6. Neither Ms. Cline nor Ms. Cline’s daughter had requested that the Elantra be towed. 
7. Ms. Cline made a payment in the amount of $250 to Rodney Dupre, Jr. through CashApp 
on October 4, 2025, at 10:19 P.M. Ms. Cline later disputed the charge and sought a refund 
through CashApp, but the refund request was denied. (Staff Exhibit 7, in globo). 
8. Upon receiving the $250 payment from Ms. Cline, Jace’s Towing unhooked the Elantra 
from the tow truck and turned the vehicle back over to Ms. Cline’s daughter. 
9. Jace’s Towing Invoice No. 563 was issued for the Elantra tow. (Staff Exhibit 7, in globo). 
10. Ms. Cline electronically submitted the Complaint to the Commission regarding the tow 
through the Commission’s complaint email (Staff Exhibit 3, in globo), prompting 
Commission Staff to initiate an investigation into Jace’s Towing. 
11. Ms. Cline filed the LSP Complaint regarding the tow. LSP conducted an investigation and 
issued the LSP Report (Staff Exhibit 4, in globo). 
12. A Hyundai Elantra’s gross vehicle weight is 10,000 pounds or less.15 
13. The average price of U.S. On-Highway Diesel Fuel as determined based upon the price 
reported by the Energy Information Administration for the Petroleum Administration for 
Gulf Coast (PADD3) on October 4, 2025, was between $3.00 and $3.99 per gallon.16 
14. On November 25, 2025, Ms. Burl issued a citation with attachments to Jace’s Towing 
directing it to appear at a hearing on February 3, 2026. (Staff Exhibit 5, in globo). 
15. Notice was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin dated December 5, 2025. 
16. The citation and its attachments were mailed to Jace’s Towing on November 25, 2025, via 
certified mail return receipt requested (receipt number ending in 613895) to the address 
last on file with the Commission when Jace’s Towing held authority, which matches the 
address on Jace’s Towing Invoice No. 563 and in the LSP Report. 
17. On January 27, 2026, the Commission’s Transportation Division received the signed 
certified mail receipt for the citation (receipt number ending in 613895), indicating that the 
certified mail was claimed. 
18. Jace’s Towing did not appear at the hearing on February 3, 2026. 
Conclusions of Law 
1. At the hearing in this matter, the Commission Staff had the burden of proving its allegations 
against Jace’s Towing. Because Jace’s Towing did not appear at the hearing, the 
Commission Staff also had the burden of demonstrating that the Carrier was provided fair 
notice of the hearing and the opportunity to present a defense.17 
2. Pursuant to its constitutional and statutory authority, the Commission adopted the Rules of 
Practice and Procedure. Commission Rules 7 and 19 provide for notice of non-criminal

proceedings through publication in the Commission’s Official Bulletin, as well as service 
“through any means whereby proof of receipt or unclaimed status can be shown” to “the 
last known place of address of the person entitled to receive such notice . . . .”18 
3. Per constitutional and legislative mandate, the Commission has the authority to regulate 
intrastate nonconsensual towing and recovery services. La. R.S. 45:180.1 provides that an 
LPSC wrecker license is required and that the Commission has authority to regulate and 
fix reasonable and just rates for the operation and use of wreckers and towing services. 
Pursuant to its authority, the Commission adopted the 1999 General Order which provides 
the application process for obtaining Commission authority to perform nonconsensual tows 
in Louisiana. The Commission also adopted the Towing Order which establishes the 
schedule of rates and terms for nonconsensual towing and recovery services. 
Per the Towing Order, the Commission issued the 2025 Towing Order Rates, which 
contains the rates and terms for services applicable to the tow that is the subject of this 
proceeding. Those rates are quoted in the Applicable Law section, above. 
4. In accordance with La. R.S. 45:171(A), no carrier shall violate the provisions of Title 45, 
Chapter 4 (which includes La. R.S. 45: 180.1) or any Commission order. La. R.S. 45:180.1 
states that in addition to any other penalties imposed by Chapter 4, no person shall violate 
Section 180.1 or engage in the operation and use of wreckers and towing services without 
first having obtained authority from the Commission. La. R.S. 45:171(C) and La. R.S. 
45:180.1(E) state that violators shall be fined by the Commission at open hearing not less 
than $100 and not more than $10,000. 
5. The Commission Staff proved, chiefly through the signed USPS certified mail return 
receipt for certified mail tracking number ending in 613895, that Jace’s Towing received 
notice of the hearing and the Commission’s allegations. Thus, the Carrier had the 
opportunity to appear and present a defense at the hearing. 
6. The Commission Staff proved that Jace’s Towing violated La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1 
and the 1999 General Order by operating intrastate without authority. Specifically, that 
Jace’s Towing conducted a nonconsensual, private property tow19 of Ms. Cline’s Hyundai 
Elantra (a light duty vehicle)20 on October 4, 2025 in Opelousas, Louisiana. Because Jace’s 
Towing conducted an intrastate, nonconsensual tow without first being registered with the 
Commission to perform such tows, Jace’s Towing violated La. R.S. 45:180.1 and the 1999 
General Order. 
7. The Commission Staff proved that Jace’s Towing violated the Towing Order by exceeding 
prescribed rates, as contained in the 2025 Towing Order Rates. The prescribed rate for a 
light duty, private property tow on October 4, 2025, would have been a flat rate of 
$146.5021 plus a fuel surcharge of 12%.22 Therefore, the prescribed rate for the Elantra tow 
is $164.08 ($146.50 plus 12%, which is $17.58, for a total of $164.08). Jace’s Towing 
charged Ms. Cline $250.00. Jace’s Towing charged Ms. Cline $85.92 in excess of the 
prescribed rate. 
8. Commission Staff requested a $1,000 fine for Jace’s Towing’s operating intrastate without 
authority, asserting that a $1,000 fine is warranted for this violation and is consistent with 
Commission precedent.23 The Commission’s practice has been to consider each case on its

reasonable defense. Considering those factors, Commission Staff’s arguments, 
Commission precedent, and the facts of this case, we find a $1,000 fine reasonable. 
9. Commission Staff requested that Jace’s Towing be ordered to refund to Ms. Cline $171.84 
for exceeding state prescribed rates.24 The Towing Order/2025 Towing Order Rates at 
Section IV(B) states, that in addition to any fines, the Commission “may order a refund of 
up to 200% of any overcharges.” The Commission Staff argued that the overcharge in this 
matter was $85.92 (the amount in excess of the prescribed rate), and that Jace’s Towing 
should be required to refund 200% of that amount, $171.84. Commission Staff’s refund 
request is reasonable based on the facts of this proceeding and Commission precedent.25 
10. Commission Staff requested that Jace’s Towing be required to pay a $25 citation fee in 
accordance with the 2006 General Order. We find the $25 citation fee is warranted. 
11. Commission Staff requested that fines and fees be paid to the Commission in certified 
funds within 30 days of any order issued in this matter. Commission Staff also requested 
that the refund in the amount of $171.84 to Ms. Cline be made in certified funds with proof 
of payment submitted to the Commission within 30 days of any order in this matter. We 
find those requests appropriate. 
Conclusion 
In accordance with the findings of fact and conclusions of law stated above, 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that: 
1. Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s Towing & Transport is guilty of violating La. R.S. 45:161 
through 180.1 and the 1999 General Order by operating intrastate without authority, 
specifically conducting a nonconsensual, private property tow on October 4, 2025, 
without LPSC authority. 

2. Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s Towing & Transport shall pay a $1,000 fine pursuant to 
La. R.S. 45:171(C) and 180.1(E) for its violation La. R.S. 45:161 through 180.1 and 
the 1999 General Order. 

3. Rodney Dupre, Jr. dba Jace’s Towing & Transport shall pay a $25 citation fee pursuant 
to the 2006 General Order. 

4. Fines and fees ordered herein shall be paid to the Commission in certified funds within
